items.abstract: <jats:p>The growing complexity of modern network infrastructures demands automation solutions that are not limited to the static scripting and traditional Software-Defined Networking (SDN) controllers. In this paper, a new, decentralized, Agentic AI, model of network engineering is presented, designed to provide intent-aware auto-remediation and active optimization. The proposed system makes use of a set of specialized autonomous agents, powered by Local Large Language Models (LLMs) and anchored by Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to read higher-level human intentions, validate them, and implement amendments. The paper introduces a strong Human-in-the-Loop architecture where the critical actions are first checked by a network simulation engine (Batfish) [2] and then approved by operators before being deployed. Its implementation, tested in resource-constrained environments, shows a feasible path towards the implementation of "NetDevOps" by integrating a Source of Truth (NetBox), Observability (Prometheus [6] / Loki), and Workflow Orchestration (n8n). The experimental findings validate the fact that the system can convert intent in natural language into valid network configurations that can support agent response times of less than 15ms and hence agility and reliability in network operations.</jats:p>
title: "The Era of AI Agents for Network Engineering": Intent-Aware Auto Remediation for Network Disruption or Failures Using AI Agents, Large Language Models (LLM) and Model Context Protocol (MCP) Mechanisms

items.abstract: <jats:p>Multi-turn jailbreak attacks, decomposing strategically malicious intent into sequences of Multi-turn jailbreak attacks, decomposing strategically malicious intent into sequences of seemingly benign queries, pose a critical security threat to large language model agents. Existing defenses, whether based on static input-filtering or rigid alignment, often fail to detect such gradual intent drift and frequently sacrifice utility through indiscriminate refusals or impaired reasoning. To address this, we propose Graph‐MDP, a novel real‐time defense framework that reformulates multi‐turn safety as dynamic state transitions over an evolving intent‐risk graph via a risk-aware Markov decision process. During interaction, Graph‐MDP performs proactive trajectory monitoring, computing a path‐based risk score that integrates node vulnerability, edge transition risks, and adversarial escalation trends. This enables adaptive safety modulation, maintaining high utility in low‐risk contexts while progressively tightening guardrails as risk accumulates. After each dialogue, an anchor-based Temporal Difference learning mechanism identifies the Risk Anchor, the pivotal turn where an attack manifests, to propagate safety rewards bidirectionally to refine risk estimation and preempt similar adversarial patterns. As a plug-and-play defense layer, Graph‐MDP requires no fine-tuning and maintains a bounded memory footprint through a node-eviction policy. Experiments on CoSafe and SafeDialBench show that Graph-MDP significantly reduces attack success rates while preserving model utility. This work establishes a scalable paradigm for securing agents against complex, long-horizon adversarial strategies.</jats:p>
title: Securing Large Language Model Agents against Multi-Turn Jailbreaks via Evolving Intent-Risk Graphs

items.abstract: <jats:p>In open-world dialogue systems, new intent discovery (NID) aims to identify previously unseen user intents from raw utterances and expand the supported intent set. This process is traditionally time-consuming and often requires domain experts to explore data and define intent labels, which substantially increases the cost. To address this challenge, we propose SCNID, a semi-supervised framework that integrates contrastive representation learning with LLM-driven pairwise-constraint-guided clustering fusion. Specifically, SCNID learns discriminative intent representations via semi-supervised contrastive learning, and then performs clustering fusion by combining a Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) with K-means++ to improve robustness and stability. Moreover, we leverage a large language model (LLM) to generate Must-Link and Cannot-Link constraints, providing structured semantic guidance for clustering. Extensive experiments on four benchmarks---three intent discovery datasets (Clinc150, Banking77, and StackOverflow20) and an additional cross-domain topic dataset (DBPedia14)---demonstrate that SCNID achieves strong and stable performance under diverse data distributions, validating the effectiveness of the proposed approach.</jats:p>
title: Application of Large Language Model-Driven Pairwise Constrained Clustering Fusion Algorithm in New Intent Discovery
